NutriBev Holdings - Q3 FY2024 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NutriBev Holdings Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. [Standard operator instructions for joining the queue.]

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson (Head of Investor Relations):
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NutriBev Holdings' Q3 FY2024 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Growth Officer; and Tom Reyes, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 FY2024. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on seven key areas: gross margin analysis, drivers and trends; impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions; e-commerce sales growth and contribution to total revenue; discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies; capital expenditure plans and priorities; EBITDA margin performance and key factors; and impact of new product innovations and launches.

On gross margins, we saw continued expansion thanks to pricing, mix, and productivity gains offsetting input costs. Mike will unpack the drivers shortly. Regarding input cost inflation and supply chain issues, our proactive hedging and diversification kept impacts contained. E-commerce remains a high-growth channel, now a significant portion of sales. Our pricing and revenue growth management delivered robust top-line results. We're ramping capex to support long-term growth priorities. EBITDA margins accelerated meaningfully. And new products are driving outsized revenue contributions.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike to provide more detail on our financial results and expand on these areas.

Mike Chen (CFO):
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 FY2024. Net sales were $1.45 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year on an organic constant-currency basis. Gross margin was 38.2%, impacted favorably by pricing and productivity but offset by commodity inflation. Operating income was $285 million, up 12% year-over-year, and diluted earnings per share were $1.12. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.2 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Let me now dive deeper into the seven areas Alex highlighted, starting with gross margin analysis, drivers, and trends. Our team delivered a Q3 gross margin of 38.2%, up 70 basis points year-over-year from 37.5% and 140 basis points sequentially from 36.8% in Q2. This marks our third consecutive quarter of margin expansion, bringing our trailing twelve-month gross margin to a robust 37.9%—well above our long-term target of 37% and positioning us favorably against peers like PepsiCo at 55% and Mondelez at 43%, adjusted for our balanced snack-and-beverage portfolio.

Key drivers included pricing actions contributing 220 basis points, with targeted increases averaging 5-7% across core categories—beverages up 6.2%, snacks 5.8%—while managing elasticity effectively. Consumer tolerance stayed strong for premium SKUs like our EverFresh organic snack line, realizing 8% price without volume loss. Favorable product mix added 110 basis points, with a 3-point shift to higher-margin branded items; ready-to-drink coffees and plant-based dairy alternatives now at 22% of beverage sales, up from 18% last year, offering 500-700 basis points above average.

Productivity initiatives from our Factory 4.0 program—AI-optimized yields and robotic palletizing in 15 of 28 North American plants—boosted efficiency by 4.2%, lowering COGS per case, alongside $45 million in year-to-date procurement savings via hedging, like locking 70% of FY2024 cocoa at $3,200 per metric ton before spot prices hit $4,100 due to West African shortfalls.

Offsetting these were input inflation shaving 180 basis points from sugar up 12% YoY, dairy proteins up 9%, palm oil up 15%; freight added 40 basis points from Red Sea issues raising Asia ocean rates 25%; and FX with a 5% stronger USD versus EUR and BRL hitting 15% of COGS.

Trends show sustained gains from 36.1% in Q3 FY2023 to 38.2%, with sequential lift from back-to-school snacks and easing energy. Beverages at 41.5% up 50 bps YoY on premium RTD, snacks at 35.8% up 120 bps, dairy at 39.2% from milk stabilization. Volume leverage in premium channels grew 4% despite headline softness.

Regionally, North America (65% sales) at 40.1% up 90 bps from private-label wins at Walmart and Kroger, plus Oatly-licensed milks. EMEA (22%) flat at 35.4% from UK energy surcharges and Turkish inflation, mitigated by Polish wheat sourcing. APAC (13%) up 150 bps to 36.7% via Indonesia palm hedging and China low-sugar Boba Boost.

Technical efforts like 80% complete ERPNext migration cut inventory costs 15% in perishables, and regenerative agriculture pilots with 20 suppliers target 10% lower inputs by FY2026. Portfolio optimization divests low-margin sugary cereals to fund $200 million in high-ROIC functional snacks. Hedging covers 65% of inputs to Q2 FY2025, with new Wisconsin dairy plant for 300 bps gains. We expect Q4 at 38.5-39.0%, FY2024 at 38.1%.

Next, the impact of input cost inflation and supply chain disruptions. These industry-wide pressures—like PepsiCo's 11% snack inflation and Nestlé's 9% escalations—limited our gross margin compression to 180 bps YoY, below initial 250 bps guidance.

Commodity inflation averaged 12.7% in Q3 from 8.2% Q2: wheat/grains up 22% from Russia-Ukraine, adding $45 million to bakery/cereal COGS; edible oils up 28% from El Niño palm/soybean hits, key for 25% of snack recipe costs; dairy/proteins +15% from U.S. milk and Europe energy; packaging/freight +11% with boxes up 14%, ocean rates +20%.

North America (45% revenue) averaged 11%, Europe (30%) 16% from gas peaks, APAC (15%) 18% palm volatility, LATAM (10%) stable on coffee/sugar. Pre-mitigation, 320 bps headwind narrowed by actions.

Fulfillment dipped to 92% from 98% YoY, above industry 88%: LA/Long Beach congestion delayed 15% Asia imports; U.S. warehouse turnover 45%; Hurricane Idalia cut Florida citrus 8%, Indian floods spices 10%.

Mitigations: hedged 75% 2024 wheat/corn 15% below spot ($120 million savings), shifted 30% palm to Malaysia; diversified vendors 25%, nearshored U.S. dairy; SAP Ariba AI forecasting cut inventory 12% to $450 million, $50 million blockchain traceability; 7-9% pricing on 60% portfolio (elasticity -2.5), mix to low-sugar drinks +15% volume; Zero Waste yielded $30 million via 3% scrap drop on chips.

Expect inflation 7-9% FY24, fulfillment 96% year-end. This cut 2.1% adjusted EPS but sets up 150 bps Q4 expansion.

Turning to e-commerce sales growth and total revenue contribution. Amid digital shifts for convenience and sustainability, e-commerce hit $210 million in Q3, 16.8% of $1.25 billion total net revenues (up 6% YoY organic, 3% volume offsetting 3% price/mix), up from 11.2% YoY and 14.5% prior quarter—a 42% YoY surge, beating U.S. online grocery 28% per Nielsen, 150% two-year stack.

DTC via NutriBev Direct: $85 million, +55% YoY, AOV $65 up 12% on subscription bundles (Organic Vitality shakes, ReadyMeal kits at 40% volume). Marketplace (Amazon, Walmart, Instacart): $125 million, +36%, GMV $160 million post 20-25% take, 2.8 SKUs/order via cross-sell like Quench with snacks.

North America 72% ($151 million) via Amazon Fresh/Walmart+ integrations, conversions to 4.2% on EcoCrunch recyclable packs. Europe 18% ($38 million) +38% on Ocado/Rewe. APAC 10% ($21 million) +62% on Tmall/ShopeeFood for GreenGlow.

Powered by AI recommendation engine on Google Cloud boosting repeats 28% from 5 million users; VMI with DoorDash/Uber Eats cut out-of-stocks <2%, costs 15%; subscription ARPU $180, churn <8%.

Margin-accretive: DTC 42% gross, 800 bps above retail; segment EBITDA 18.2% up 220 bps. Data drove Vitality reformulation +25% repeats. Target 22-25% revenues by FY2025, $50 million capex for micro-fulfillment.

Challenges: CAC $18, cocoa volatility, competition—but omnichannel positions us for 20-25% F&B online penetration per McKinsey.

On pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies, these drove 6.2% organic growth, outpacing industry 3-4% per NielsenIQ/IRI, despite cocoa +45%, sugar +12%, dairy +8%.

Pricing contributed 5.1 points (from 3.8 Q2), volume/mix +1.1; net realization +6.8%, trade spend 18.2% down 50 bps.

List increases 7-9%: beverages 8.2% on VitaFizz (92% pass-through, elasticity -1.8), energy 9.5% (-1.4); snacks 7.4%, chips 8.1%, cookies 6.9% with shrinkflation <2%; dairy 6.5%, VitaPro +3.2% volume.

RGM via RevOptix AI (SymphonyAI, 2.5PB POS data): premiumization to 28% revenue (+0.8 ppt from OatVita); promo reset -22% deep discounts, ROI 1.7x; innovation $45 million zero-sugar VitaFizz; dynamic e-com +2.3 ppt.

North America (55%) +7.2%, pricing +6.4%; Europe (20%) +5.1%, +7.1%; APAC (15%) +4.8%, China +8.9%; LATAM (10%) +3.9%.

Guide 4-6% pricing FY24, 7-9% organic; hedged 70% cocoa, AI scenario planning.

Capital expenditure plans and priorities: FY2024 $2.2 billion (4.2% sales, 15% ROIC); FY2025 $2.5 billion (+14%), FY2026 $2.7 billion, at 2.1x net debt/EBITDA.

Priority 1 (40%, $1.0B): manufacturing, $450 million aseptic lines for VitaGlow (+25% output, 18-24 month payback); NA brownfields, Vietnam greenfield, Brazil beverages.

Priority 2 (25%, $625M): supply chain $300M cold chain DCs (spoilage <2%), $325M Industry 4.0 AI maintenance (downtime -30%).

Priority 3 (20%, $500M): ESG $250M water zero-discharge, $150M renewables (50% emissions cut), $100M rPET packaging.

Priority 4 (15%, $375M): R&D Singapore CoE upcycled ingredients, lab automation for collagen coffee.

14-16% IRR, 200 bps EBITDA to 22% FY2027; modular designs, hedges.

EBITDA margin expanded 150 bps to 22.5%, organic 22.8%, ahead of 21.5% guide. Gross +220 bps from 4.5% pricing (beverages 5.2%, snacks 4.8%); supply chain $45 million (110 bps, Precision Sourcing AI hedging cocoa/dairy); SG&A leverage 80 bps (12.1% flat, SAP S/4HANA -18% spend).

NA 25.2% +280 bps, EMEA 19.8% +90 bps plant-based, APAC 23.1% +120 bps RTD tea. Headwinds: inflation $120 million (60 bps), FX 40 bps.

Premium Core: 85% high-growth SKUs; FY24 guide 21.8-22.3%.

Finally, new product innovations and launches: NPD (24 months) 18% revenue (+ from 12%), +3.2 ppt to 8% organic growth, $285 million +28% YoY, 65% repeat velocity vs. 45% benchmark.

Beverages: VitaBoost Zero-Sugar $112 million (+15% forecast), 52% margins HPP Arizona. Snacks: KetoCrunch $68 million, 4.2% share, Costco velocity 8.2, PCR packaging.

NA 62% $177 million ACV 87%; Europe 22% $63 million Matcha Lattes; APAC 45% $32 million localized; LATAM +14%.

R&D 2.8% sales, AI flavors; cannibalization <8%. H2 22 SKUs $650 million; mid-teens growth to 12-15% CAGR.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 6-8% and EPS of $4.50-$4.80.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

John Smith (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of input cost inflation on your business?

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thanks, John. As Mike detailed, we saw 12.7% average inflation, led by grains 22%, oils 28%, dairy 15%, but hedging 75% of wheat/corn, supplier diversification, and pricing recovered most, limiting to 180 bps gross pressure. We're positioned for moderation ahead.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your plans for new products like VitaBoost and what is the expected impact?

Lisa Patel (Chief Growth Officer):
Thanks, Emily. VitaBoost exceeded forecasts at $112 million, driving 3.2 ppt organic growth with 52% margins and 65% repeats. Our pipeline of 22 SKUs targets $650 million H2, mid-teens growth supporting premiumization and 12-15% innovation CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

David Lee (Morgan Stanley):
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

Tom Reyes (Chief Supply Chain Officer):
Good question, David. Fulfillment at 92%, with AI forecasting, VMI partnerships cutting costs 15%, five new DCs, and blockchain traceability. Diversification and nearshoring rebound us to 96% by year-end, ahead of industry.

Operator:
Our last question comes from Rachel Kim with Barclays. Please proceed.

Rachel Kim (Barclays):
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

Mike Chen (CFO):
Thanks, Rachel. Q4 gross 38.5-39.0%, EBITDA 21.8-22.3% FY24, supported by pricing 4-6%, productivity $150 million, hedged inputs, and e-com ramp. Organic sales 6-8%, resilient amid macro.

Operator:
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex for closing remarks.

Alex Rivera (CEO):
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in NutriBev Holdings. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
